problems.title: One-step then divide
hints: Undo the **+5** first — subtract 5 from both sides.
Then undo the **×2** — divide both sides by 2.
problems.solution:
Peel off the added term first, then the coefficient:

$$2x + 5 = 17$$
$$2x = 17 - 5 = 12 \quad(\text{subtract 5 from both sides})$$
$$x = \frac{12}{2} = 6 \quad(\text{divide both sides by 2})$$

Check: $2(6) + 5 = 17$ ✓.

problems.title: Solve for acceleration
problems.scenario:
The equation $v = u + at$ links velocity, initial velocity, acceleration and time.

Given $v = 20$, $u = 5$ and $t = 3$, find $a$.
hints: First rearrange: subtract $u$, then divide by $t$ → $a = (v-u)/t$.
Substitute $v=20,\,u=5,\,t=3$.
problems.solution:
Rearrange for $a$, then substitute:

$$v = u + at \;\Rightarrow\; a = \frac{v - u}{t}$$
$$a = \frac{20 - 5}{3} = \frac{15}{3} = 5$$

Doing the algebra *before* plugging in numbers keeps it clean and reusable.

problems.title: Make a the subject
problems.scenario:
Make $a$ the subject of

$$v = u + at$$

Write the rearranged formula.
hints: The term $at$ is added — remove $u$ from both sides first.
Then $a$ is multiplied by $t$ — divide both sides by $t$.
problems.solution:
Undo the addition, then the multiplication:

$$v = u + at$$
$$v - u = at \quad(\text{subtract } u)$$
$$a = \frac{v - u}{t} \quad(\text{divide by } t)$$

problems.title: Density: find the mass
problems.scenario:
Density is $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V}$.

A fluid has density $\rho = 800\ \text{kg/m}^3$ in a volume $V = 0.5\ \text{m}^3$. Find the mass $m$, in kg.
hints: $m$ is divided by $V$ — multiply both sides by $V$.
$m = \rho V$.
problems.solution:
Multiply both sides by $V$ to free $m$:

$$\rho = \frac{m}{V} \;\Rightarrow\; m = \rho V$$
$$m = 800 \times 0.5 = 400\ \text{kg}$$

problems.title: Variable in the denominator
hints: $V$ is underneath — multiply both sides by $V$ first to lift it up.
Then divide both sides by $\rho$.
problems.solution:
Lift $V$ out of the denominator, then isolate it:

$$\rho = \frac{m}{V}$$
$$\rho V = m \quad(\text{multiply both sides by } V)$$
$$V = \frac{m}{\rho} \quad(\text{divide both sides by } \rho)$$

problems.title: Spot the correct rearrangement
problems.scenario: The area of a circle is $A = \pi r^2$. Which correctly makes $r$ the subject?
hints: First divide both sides by $\pi$ to get $r^2$ alone.
Then take the square root of both sides — the inverse of squaring.
problems.solution:
Divide by $\pi$, then square-root:

$$A = \pi r^2 \;\Rightarrow\; \frac{A}{\pi} = r^2 \;\Rightarrow\; r = \sqrt{\frac{A}{\pi}}$$

The square root undoes the square; you apply it to the *whole* of $A/\pi$.

problems.title: Circle area: find the radius
problems.scenario: A circle has area $A = 50.27\ \text{m}^2$. Using $A = \pi r^2$, find its radius $r$, in m.
hints: Rearrange to $r = \sqrt{A/\pi}$.
$A/\pi \approx 16$, and $\sqrt{16} = 4$.
problems.solution:
Rearrange, then substitute:

$$r = \sqrt{\frac{A}{\pi}} = \sqrt{\frac{50.27}{3.1416}} = \sqrt{16.0} = 4\ \text{m}$$

Keep the positive root — a radius can't be negative.

problems.title: Ideal gas: make T the subject
problems.scenario:
The ideal-gas law is $pV = nRT$.

Make $T$ the subject.
hints: $T$ is multiplied by $n$ and by $R$ on the right.
Divide both sides by the product $nR$.
problems.solution:
$T$ is multiplied by both $n$ and $R$, so divide both sides by their product:

$$pV = nRT \;\Rightarrow\; T = \frac{pV}{nR}$$

Everything that multiplied $T$ moves underneath as a division.

problems.title: Kinetic energy: find the speed
problems.scenario:
Kinetic energy is $KE = \tfrac{1}{2} m v^2$.

A body of mass $m = 2\ \text{kg}$ has $KE = 100\ \text{J}$. Find its speed $v$, in m/s.
hints: Rearrange: $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\,KE}{m}}$ (multiply by 2, divide by $m$, then root).
problems.solution:
Undo the $\tfrac12$ and $m$, then the square:

$$KE = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \;\Rightarrow\; v^2 = \frac{2\,KE}{m} \;\Rightarrow\; v = \sqrt{\frac{2\,KE}{m}}$$
$$v = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 100}{2}} = \sqrt{100} = 10\ \text{m/s}$$

problems.title: Variable on both sides
hints: Collect the $x$ terms on one side — subtract $2x$ from both sides.
Then deal with the constant, and divide by the coefficient.
problems.solution:
Gather the unknowns, then isolate:

$$5x - 3 = 2x + 9$$
$$3x - 3 = 9 \quad(\text{subtract } 2x)$$
$$3x = 12 \quad(\text{add } 3)$$
$$x = 4 \quad(\text{divide by } 3)$$

Check: $5(4)-3 = 17$ and $2(4)+9 = 17$ ✓.

problems.title: Pendulum: make L the subject
problems.scenario:
The period of a pendulum is

$$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}.$$

Make $L$ the subject.
hints: Divide both sides by $2\pi$ to isolate the square root.
Square both sides to remove the root, then multiply by $g$.
problems.solution:
Strip the $2\pi$, undo the root by squaring, then free $L$:

$$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$$
$$\frac{T}{2\pi} = \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} \quad(\text{divide by } 2\pi)$$
$$\left(\frac{T}{2\pi}\right)^2 = \frac{L}{g} \quad(\text{square both sides})$$
$$L = g\left(\frac{T}{2\pi}\right)^2 \quad(\text{multiply by } g)$$

problems.title: Parallel resistors
problems.scenario:
Two resistors in parallel satisfy $\dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{1}{R_1} + \dfrac{1}{R_2}$.

With $R_1 = 3\ \Omega$ and $R_2 = 6\ \Omega$, find the combined resistance $R$, in Ω.
hints: Add the right-hand fractions over a common denominator first.
You'll get $1/R$; the unknown is in the denominator, so take the reciprocal at the end.
problems.solution:
Combine the fractions, then invert (the variable is in the denominator):

$$\frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{2}{6} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$R = 2\ \Omega$$

Because $1/R = 1/2$, taking the reciprocal of both sides gives $R = 2$.

problems.title: Isolate a variable under a root
hints: The whole right side is under a root — square both sides first to remove it.
Then $b^2$ is added to $a^2$; subtract $a^2$, and root last.
problems.solution:
Square to kill the root, then isolate $b$ and root once at the end:

$$c = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$$
$$c^2 = a^2 + b^2 \quad(\text{square both sides})$$
$$b^2 = c^2 - a^2 \quad(\text{subtract } a^2)$$
$$b = \sqrt{c^2 - a^2} \quad(\text{take the root})$$

Square first (to undo the given root), then root last (to free $b$) — the two roots are doing different jobs.

problems.title: Variable in a denominator with a sum
hints: $x$ is buried in the denominator — multiply both sides by $(b + x)$ to lift it out.
You get $y(b + x) = a$; isolate the $(b+x)$ group, then subtract $b$.
$b + x = a/y$.
problems.solution:
Lift the whole denominator, then peel it apart:

$$y = \frac{a}{b + x}$$
$$y(b + x) = a \quad(\text{multiply by } b + x)$$
$$b + x = \frac{a}{y} \quad(\text{divide by } y)$$
$$x = \frac{a}{y} - b \quad(\text{subtract } b)$$

The trick is treating $(b+x)$ as a single block until it's out of the denominator.

problems.title: Variable on both sides (in a fraction)
problems.scenario:
Make $x$ the subject of

$$\frac{x - a}{x + a} = k.$$
hints: Clear the fraction first: multiply both sides by $(x + a)$.
Now $x$ appears on both sides — expand, then collect all $x$ terms on one side.
Factor $x$ out: $x(1 - k) = a(1 + k)$.
problems.solution:
Clear the fraction, gather the $x$'s, then factor and divide:

$$\frac{x - a}{x + a} = k$$
$$x - a = k(x + a) \quad(\text{multiply by } x + a)$$
$$x - a = kx + ka$$
$$x - kx = a + ka \quad(\text{collect } x \text{ on the left})$$
$$x(1 - k) = a(1 + k) \quad(\text{factor out } x)$$
$$x = \frac{a(1 + k)}{1 - k} \quad(\text{divide by } 1 - k)$$

When the unknown appears twice, factoring it out so it appears once is the move that unlocks it.
